commentary.text: I’m establishing an early central foothold with Red at (3,3), aiming to pair it with Yellow on a second center square and contest the instant-win zone before Blue and Green can coordinate there.
I’m taking a safe central foothold with Blue at (4,4). It advances the center-victory plan without placing Blue in an immediate Red sandwich, while restricting Yellow’s movement along column 4.
Yellow joins Red in the center at (4,3), securing a second central square and preparing Red to occupy (3,4). Blue’s piece at (4,4) remains the key obstacle to a center victory.

I’m placing Green at (2,4) to block Red’s direct descent along column 4 and establish a same-color flank above the center. If Blue vacates (4,4), a later Green move to (5,4) can punish an opposing piece that enters (3,4).

I’m placing Red at (1,4) behind Green’s advanced piece. This sets up a Red move from (3,3) to (3,4) that would sandwich and capture Green at (2,4), while preserving Yellow’s threat to capture Blue at (4,4).

I’m shifting Blue from (4,4) to the upper center at (3,4), escaping Yellow’s immediate sandwich threat via (4,5). Red could threaten it from (3,5), so Green should be ready to obstruct the Red piece’s descent along column 5.
Yellow takes (4,4), giving Team A three central squares. Red can next attack Blue at (3,4) by moving from (0,5) to (3,5), sandwiching it against Red at (3,3).

I’m moving Green to (2,5) to block Red’s route from (0,5) to (3,5), which would otherwise sandwich and capture Blue at (3,4) against Red at (3,3). This preserves our central foothold while keeping Green mobile near the center.

I’m moving Red to (3,6), creating an immediate threat to step into (3,5) and sandwich Blue’s center piece at (3,4) against Red at (3,3). This pressures Blue to abandon the center while Team A holds the other three central squares.
Blue exploits the same-color flank on row 3: moving into (3,5) sandwiches Red at (3,6) against Blue at (3,7), scoring Red’s first loss while preserving our advanced formation.
Yellow steps into the vacated center square at (3,4), completing Team A’s occupation of all four central squares for the immediate win.

I’m advancing Green to (5,4) as a safe central staging piece. It can contest (4,4) later, while the Green at (2,5) continues shielding Blue’s upper-center position and obstructing Red’s column-5 route.
The center was not yet complete because (4,4) remains empty. Red advances to (4,2), preparing to cross into (4,4) once Yellow vacates (4,3), while keeping Red’s existing center anchor at (3,3).

Yellow threatens to complete the center on its next turn. Blue has no legal route to a central square or immediate capture that prevents it, so I’m placing Blue at (4,7) to preserve mobility and prepare a path toward row 4 if play continues.
Yellow shifts from (4,3) to (4,4), completing Team A’s occupation of all four central squares alongside Red at (3,3) and Yellow at (3,4), for an immediate center victory.

Green springs the prepared vertical sandwich: moving to (2,4) traps both central Yellow pieces against Green at (5,4). This removes Yellow from (3,4) and (4,4), decisively stopping Team A’s center threat and inflicting two Yellow losses.

Red steps to (3,4), sandwiching and capturing Green at (2,4) against Red at (1,4). This removes the invader that just broke our center formation while keeping a Red piece on a central square; Yellow is now one loss from elimination, so its remaining pieces must be handled cautiously.

I’m staging Blue at (2,3) to threaten a decisive move to (3,3), which would sandwich Red at (3,4) against Blue at (3,5). This forces Red to abandon or defend the center while Green remains poised to occupy (4,4).
Yellow advances toward the remaining center squares while staying clear of immediate sandwich threats. From (4,5), it can contest (4,4) next turn and support rebuilding Team A’s center formation.

I’m occupying (4,4) with Green, securing a central square while preserving the tactical plan: Blue still threatens (3,3) to capture Red at (3,4), and if Red moves from (4,2) into (4,3), Green can later sandwich it between Green pieces at (4,2) and (4,4).

Red shifts to (0,6), threatening to descend to (3,6) and sandwich Blue at (3,5) against Red at (3,4). This forces Blue to move the exposed piece or block column 6, buying time to address Green’s occupation of (4,4).
Blue executes the prepared tactic: moving to (3,3) sandwiches Red at (3,4) against Blue at (3,5), inflicting Red’s second loss and strengthening our grip on the center.

Yellow shifts along the back rank to (7,3), preparing to rise to (4,3) and sandwich Green at (4,4) against Yellow at (4,5). This forces Green to address the capture threat or abandon its central foothold; both Red and Yellow remain one loss from elimination.

Green advances to (6,3), blocking Yellow at (7,3) from reaching (4,3) and capturing our central Green. It also creates a direct center threat: after Blue occupies (3,4), this Green can move to (4,3) to complete Team B’s four-square center occupation. If Red blocks with (4,2)–(4,3), Green can answer (4,0)–(4,2), sandwiching Red against Green at (4,4) for Red’s third loss.

Red moves to (3,2), creating a direct sandwich threat: next Red can land at (3,4) and capture Blue at (3,3) against this new flank. This pressures Blue to abandon or defend the central square while Yellow prepares to dislodge Green from (4,4).

Blue closes the upper half of the center by sliding to (3,4). Together with Blue at (3,3) and Green at (4,4), this creates an immediate center-victory threat: Green at (6,3) can move through (5,3) to (4,3) on our next turn unless Yellow finds a defense.

Yellow advances from the back rank to (4,2), creating a clear next-turn route to (4,3), where it could sandwich Green at (4,4) against Yellow at (4,5). The piece remains safe from an immediate Green sandwich because the gap at (4,3) breaks Green’s potential flank.
Green completes Team B’s center occupation by moving from (6,3) to (4,3), joining Blue at (3,3) and (3,4) and Green at (4,4) for an immediate victory.
